doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Ideas away from work
summary: Hey hears riffs in passing and likes to step away from a track and think about the part.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you get ideas in your head even when you’re not really engaged in working? I guess I think I saw your dog come through the room. And when I take my dog for a walk if I’m working on an arrangement I get these things — you know I’m thinking more about how am I going to solve this little issue. I wonder if this happens to you?

It kind of, in passing if I hear something — the other day I heard some vocal riff that was — wow that was really cool. How can we make that, how can I make that into a horn part that works you know. Stuff like that. But if I’m kind of working on a song and I used to like to listen to it, work on it, then, you know, take a walk and then without hearing the track kind of think okay here’s sort of the — what about this — and then come back and kind of refine that.
